metadata.title: How Small Can Anything Get?
metadata.series_style: REUSED ENGINE: video 16's Speed Ladder flipped downward as 'Scale Well'
metadata.timing_basis: MEASURED (foundation): every scene boundary after sc01 = its anchor word's measured onset - 2 frames (align_narration.py, the clean WAVs); the film = 0.5 s lead + 46.64 s narration to the release of 'one.' (47.03 s) + 1.5 s settle. Planned values kept in planned_total_*.
metadata.build_mode: LEAN: copy video 16's per-video files and pipeline scripts; flip the ladder (L = -log10 metres, top = 1 mm); new devices: eye/light-limit dashed lines, drawn atom + nucleus, electron bracket, rail break + Planck line, typed 34-zero readout. Reuse video 16's SFX X1-X6 (no new SFX spend). build_spec.py for builders and QA; qa_auto.py; 1 targeted QA agent.

taste_profile.design_read: Youth science short: a calm climb up one speed ladder, from walking to light, ending at a wall that never moves.
taste_profile.palette_discipline: Night ink sky, steel rail, ONE white-cyan accent for the marker; no temperature colours; red only for 'c' (the wall).
taste_profile.layout_variation: Log rail + marker, zeros counter, window plates, the LHC nines readout.
taste_profile.reference_strategy: Numbers from the brief only; AI stills as short tagged inserts.
anti_patterns: 'the falcon is the fastest animal' as fact without the dive caveat
quality_gates: Every rung's number matches the brief

typography.data: video 13's mono face (numbers, counter, readout; slashed zeros)

rail.note: spine x 250, L = -log10(m): y = 380 + (L - 3) * 620 / 15; decade powers right-aligned at x 224; the break y 1012-1040; the Planck line y 1080

rung_labels.note: chips de-overlapped top-down with leaders; never under the open window (build_props asserts)

reference_labels.note: 'YOUR EYE' / 'LIGHT MICROSCOPE' left of the rail (the decade powers under them are hidden)

window.note: S1 sand, S2 blood cells, S3 virus, then the DRAWN atom

counter.note: the ZEROS chip, right-aligned at x 920

metadata.signature_device: One log-scale speed rail in km/h (1 to 10^9) with a single glowing marker that climbs rung by rung while a ZEROS counter ticks 0 -> 9; the top is a red 'c' line the marker approaches but never touches; streak length = log10(speed).
hero_beats: sc05 'YOU' jumps from WALK to Earth's orbit (~107,000)
sc11 the LHC nines fill while the gap under 'c' stays
metadata.honesty_grammar: MEASURED solid tab (sand, hair, cell, virus, atom, proton, electron's upper bound); PROBABLY outline + hatch (the naked-eye limit); MAYBE dashed ghost (the Planck length as a floor, from 'Below that,' to the end of s5); IDLE at the CTA. AI plates S1-S3 tagged 'AI impression'; the atom is 'drawn · not to scale'. The rail is labelled 'metres · log scale'.

music.prompt: Instrumental bed for a curious, uplifting science short about speed, from walking pace to the speed of light, 58 seconds, about 100 BPM, D major. A light, steady texture from the very first beat: soft synth pulse, plucked strings and a gentle shimmering pad. Keep the same instruments, density and loudness from 0 to about 52 seconds: no intro build, no drop, no breakdown, no hits, no risers, no fade, no silence, no drums. Then in the last 6 seconds play one clear resolved final cadence (IV - V - I) and end on a single sustained major chord that rings out naturally for about 3 seconds.
music.alignment: find the final tonic attack from the audio (lesson 26); align ~0.15 s after 'way'; flatten level steps; duck -13 dB from 'But' (lesson 44); 0.6 s end fade (lesson 43); write ending.closing_min_margin_db (lesson 49)
